::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
A Wikipedia cross-check correction: TI Chengdu is NOT a 300mm fab (that common claim conflates the 2017 300mm bumping line). It is TI's 200mm analog fab, bought in October 2010 from Cension — which SMIC had been operating — plus back-end sites, under a 15-year strategy worth up to $1.69 billion; CDAT2 assembly/test entered production after November 2022.
:::

**Chinese name:** 德州仪器半导体制造（成都）有限公司 (Dézhōu Yíqì Chéngdū)

## What does this facility make?

Analog and power management chips for industrial/automotive markets; packaging and test for TI products.

## Why does it matter?

The main foreign-owned wafer fab in western China and the clearest counter-example to the 'foreign majors are exiting China' narrative in 2025-26: while TI closes 150mm fabs in the US/Europe, its Chengdu integrated site stays in production, and the tracker's Chengdu cluster (Intel ATP + TI fab) now matches what actually exists.

## Project Timeline

- **Oct 2010** — TI opens its first China manufacturing plant — 200mm fab acquired from Cension (ex-SMIC-operated)
- **Apr 2017** — 300mm wafer-bumping (not a wafer fab) facility announced
- **Nov 2022** — CDAT2 assembly/test site announced entering production; second A/T building completed 2021-08
